finding: Kentucky deer, structured from 301 KAR 2:172 — the seasons are STATEWIDE and only the limits are per zone
authority: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Fish and Wildlife Commission)

instrument.citation: 301 KAR 2:172, Deer hunting seasons, zones, and requirements
instrument.effectiveAs: 52 Ky.R. 479; eff. 3-3-2026 — the last entry in the regulation's own HISTORY
instrument.versionEstablishedBy: The engrossed text. The page also carries a pre-engrossment ALTERNATE VIEW whose Zone 1 has 51 counties rather than 68; the 68-county list is inside <ins data-added="1"> and the 51 inside <del data-removed="1">.

theStructuralFACT.statement: KENTUCKY'S ZONES DO NOT CHANGE THE DATES. Section 5 is headed “Statewide Season Dates” and every window in it is stated statewide; Section 7 is headed “Season and Zone Limits” and is where the zone enters.
theStructuralFACT.whyItMatters: This is §8's ‘a season is not a date range’ in its cleanest form. Flattening Kentucky to ‘deer season: September – January’ would be true of the dates and useless: the legal opportunity differs by zone in LIMITS and, in Zone 4, in WHICH IMPLEMENT may take an antlerless deer at all. Two zones with identical dates are different opportunities.
theStructuralFACT.soTheRuleSHAPE: Each opportunity is zone × implement × animal class, with the dates shared across zones and the limit and implement restrictions carried per zone.

seasonWindows_section5.statedAs: beginning the second Saturday in November for sixteen (16) consecutive days
During any season in which a modern gun may be used to take deer
seasonWindows_section5.note: A derived window rather than a stated one: it tracks 5(2) and any other modern-gun season.
A hunter-class-specific window two weeks longer than 5(4). This is a dimension of the opportunity, and it is the authority's own distinction.

seasonWindows_section5.licenceWaived: Shall not be required to have a hunting license or deer permit

antleredCeiling.statedAs: A person shall not take more than one (1) antlered deer per license year, regardless of permit type used or zone hunted

Zone 1.condition: if the person has purchased the appropriate additional deer permits

Zone 3.implementRestriction: a firearm or air gun shall not be used to take a total of more than one (1) antlerless deer

onlyDuring: Archery season, except not during modern gun season, the October muzzleloader season, or the first six (6) days of the December muzzleloader season
Crossbow season, with the same exceptions
The last three (3) days of the December muzzleloader season
Zone 4.note: Zone 4 is the case that proves the point: identical dates to Zone 1, and an antlerless deer is lawful only on four named occasions.

licence.statedAs: Unless license exempt, as established in KRS 150.170, a person who is hunting deer shall carry a valid: (a) Kentucky hunting license; and (b) Deer permit.
licence.youth: a Kentucky youth hunting license and a youth deer permit

hunterOrange.when: During the modern gun deer season, muzzle-loader season, and any youth gun season
hunterOrange.who: a person hunting ANY SPECIES during daylight hours and any person accompanying a hunter
hunterOrange.what: solid, unbroken hunter orange visible from all sides on the head, back, and chest
minimums: May display a small section of another color
Shall not have mesh weave openings exceeding one-fourth (1/4) inch by any measurement
A camouflage-pattern hunter orange garment worn without additional solid hunter orange on the head, back, and chest shall not meet the requirements
hunterOrange.note: The orange requirement is triggered by the DEER seasons and binds a person hunting any species, so it reaches hunters who are not hunting deer at all.

notEncodedAndWHY: Nothing here is a certified bundle. These are the structured facts a bundle needs; the bundle itself is not written.

THE ENGINE CANNOT YET ROUTE TO A COMPOSED UNIT. A ConditionalBundle's geography takes `ghas`, `gbhz`, `special` or `jurisdiction`; Kentucky's deer zone is a composed unit (`composed-units.ts`) and is none of those. Making Kentucky answer needs either that contract extended or a derived zone layer, and the first touches shared code several lanes read.

Relative dates are stated rather than resolved here: ‘the third Monday in January’ is kept as the authority's phrase, because the repository already has relative-date machinery and resolving a date twice is how two answers diverge.
Sections 1, 3, 8–14 (definitions, hunter restrictions, youth supervision, harvest recording, checking, transport, antlers, CWD surveillance) are unread here and are not claimed as absent.
